title: the DPB walk writes ref_src[16], which is the first element of the next struct member
live_proof: LIVE: the fix's 'if (nb_refs >= HEVC_MAX_REFS)' guard is absent from n9.0.1:libavcodec/vulkan_hevc.c, where the walk 'for (int i = 0; i < FF_ARRAY_ELEMS(l->DPB); i++)' still reaches the unguarded vk_hevc_fill_pict call at :760 with 'int idx = nb_refs;'. The targets are HEVC_MAX_REFS wide (:123-125) while l->DPB is HEVCFrame DPB[32] (hevcdec.h:453), so idx can reach 31.
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Sub-object spatial row.
shape: pointer array written past its end into the next member of the same allocation
allocator_layer: av_refstruct over av_malloc: one allocation for the whole picture-private struct
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. Reduced to the FIRST crossing write, ref_src[16]. Writing all sixteen extra entries the DPB[32] walk permits would run 128 bytes into a 64-byte member and leave the allocation, which is a different claim -- the first attempt at this case did exactly that and the containment check refused it, which is why the reduction is stated here rather than assumed.
distinguishing: the bound crossed FIRST is the sub-object one. Far past it the walk leaves the struct as well, so unlike case 1 this row's containment holds only for the first crossing, and the case asserts the far end of the neighbouring member survives.

spatial.oracle: the sequence completes. NOTHING WE HAVE CATCHES THIS, and measuring that is the row's purpose. The crossing is between two members of ONE allocation, so every per-allocation bound -- shrink, sublet, the pool arms, CHERI -- is in bounds for it. The authority that would have to be narrowed is per struct member, which means the compiler or the allocation site, not an allocator. That is the taxonomy's partial-squared cell, where table6-cheri-vs-capstone-explained.md already gives CHERI and Capstone the same verdict. ALSO MEASURED 2026-10-09 as this corpus's own case.c in an application domain (results/2026-10-09-capstone/): NOT CAUGHT, VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED the DPB walk wrote ref_src[16], which is h265_refs[0], inside one refstruct allocation; fixed run VERDICT FIXED.
spatial.note: Measured as probe case 42 of ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/security-tests (pool-lifetime-probes.c), which is how pool-repros measures its own Capstone arms. The probe ASSERTS the crossing happened -- the neighbouring member's sentinel must change and its far end must survive -- so a completion is a measurement and not a quiet nothing. verify-outcomes.py's fault predicate deliberately does not list these cases, because a crossing inside one allocation is in bounds for every per-allocation bound.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON: the sequence COMPLETES on both arms and each prints its own VERDICT, so the completion is a reading and not a silent pass. NOT CAUGHT. 22 of 22 arms passed, runner exit 0, with the platform controls firing in the SAME boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY. THE REASON IS WEAKER THAN 'CHERI BOUNDS THE ALLOCATION AND THE CROSSING STAYS INSIDE', and that is stated rather than glossed: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 bumps a cursor and returns a raw interior pointer, rounding every request to 64 bytes), so there is no per-allocation bound on the struct at all on this harness. The completion shows that nothing bounded anything at this granularity, not that a bound was in force and held. The sub-object claim does not rest on the arm -- the case asserts its own offsets. This is the over-claim that was corrected on the wmem arms, written down before it could be made again. BUILD: clang -O0, purecap, linked against the port's libffmpeg-pool.a from `cmake --preset cheribsd`. -O0 IS LOAD-BEARING: a first suite built -O1 returned VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE for case 0 while the other nineteen arms passed and both controls fired, because case 0's index is a compile-time constant one past its member and clang folded the store away. Rebuilt at -O0 with nothing else changed, it reads DEFECT-REPRODUCED. Reporting the -O1 suite would have recorded a compiler artifact as a CheriBSD reading. Evidence: results/20261006-cheribsd/.

native-detect.oracle: NO ASan report, MEASURED two-sided. The member-to-member crossing is inside one allocation, so there is no redzone to poison; a write one uint16_t PAST the same allocation is the positive control and ASan does report it (heap-buffer-overflow, exit 1). Without that control the silence would say nothing about the subject and something about the instrument -- and the first build of the probe proved the point: at -O1 the control was silent too, because the dead store had been optimised away.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm's write crosses into the neighbouring member and the sentinel there changes; the fixed arm's bound keeps every write inside its own member. This pair differs by the upstream fix, not by protection -- which is the ONLY oracle available for this class.

backing.oracle: not applicable, and recorded rather than omitted: there is no backing allocation distinct from the object. The object IS one av_malloc (av_refstruct_allocz -> refstruct.c:109, av_malloc(size + REFCOUNT_OFFSET)), so the 'a mechanism at the wrong point' distinction this arm draws for the pool corpus has nothing to separate here.
